description: Close this project's open regression alert(s) once you have judged them, so the analysis stops re-raising them and stops re-queuing the owner's task. Call it with `verdict:"fixed"` when the alert was RIGHT — the code really had that problem — and you fixed it, and with `verdict:"dismissed"` when you CHECKED IT AND IT WAS WRONG — a false alarm, already handled, or about code that is deliberately that way. If the SAME commit that raised the alert already handles the risk, that is `dismissed` (already handled), not `fixed`: `fixed` means the alert caught something that was really wrong. Refuting is as valuable as confirming: the accuracy this product reports needs both, and an alert you silently confirm to get rid of it makes that number a lie. Identify the alert by `module` plus `quote`: a phrase of at least 12 characters copied from the text of the alert you judged. Only alerts whose text contains it are closed, so you cannot close one you did not read; narrow further with `symbol` (the evidence symbol the alert hangs on). Judge only what you actually looked at; it is reversible from the web. project: the repo you are working in (folder name or slug).

quote.description: REQUIRED. A phrase copied from the text of the alert you judged (case, accents and punctuation do not matter). Only open alerts whose text contains it are closed.

verdict.description: REQUIRED. fixed = the alert was right: the code really had that problem and you fixed it. dismissed = you checked it and it was wrong (false alarm, already handled, or deliberate). There is no default on purpose: closing an alert without judging it would count as the generator being right and inflate the accuracy this product publishes.
